info.title: Vendor Service — Section 14 generic Inventory
info.description:
Section 14 generic Inventory authority: inventory item identity and stock basis, balances, lots, an append-only movement ledger, all-or-nothing reservations, goods receiving, stocktakes, branch transfers, quarantine, reorder rules and alerts.

Inventory owns stock truth. Shop remains the owner of products, variants, listings and catalogue measurement configuration, and keeps its own Section 12B inventory surface for compatibility; the two are bridged by inventory item identity rather than merged.

PostgreSQL is authoritative for every quantity in this document. Redis is not consulted for stock truth and its absence cannot change a balance. Available quantity never goes negative, expired and quarantined stock is never sellable, and movement rows are immutable.

Out of scope, by section: suppliers, purchase orders and goods procurement (Section 15); ingredients, recipes, production and costing (Section 16); commerce orders, checkout, payment and logistics (Section 17 and later). Reorder rules raise a restocking signal only and never create a purchase order.

get.summary: Read item availability for a trusted service
get.description: Branch-bound availability for an internal consumer such as checkout. Internal route: HMAC v2 signed, restricted to an explicit caller allowlist, and protected by durable nonce replay consumption. The Vendor tenant is derived from the authenticated caller and the branch from the path; a request body can never assert either.

get.description: Append-only stock evidence, newest first. Movement rows are immutable: the database refuses any update or delete, so corrections arrive as new movements rather than edits.

get.description: Monotonic revision for one branch. Consumers cache against it and re-read when it moves.

get.description: Balance for a single generic inventory item. An item belonging to another business, or outside the caller's branch scope, is indistinguishable from one that does not exist.

put.description: Minimum and target quantities that drive low-stock and out-of-stock alerting. Section 14 raises the signal only; purchasing belongs to Section 15.

get.description: Whether the item can currently be sold, with the reason when it cannot. Expired and quarantined stock is never sellable.

post.description: Removes stock from sellability without destroying it. Quarantining more than the available physical stock is refused.
Permanently removes quarantined stock and appends the matching controlled-loss movement evidence.
Returns quarantined stock to availability, provided it has not expired in the meantime.

Holds stock for every requested line or none of them. Reservations are idempotent on (source_type, source_ref): repeating a request with the same fingerprint returns the current durable reservation state, while the same reference with a different fingerprint is a conflict.

get.description: Current reservation state and its per-line allocations.

post.description: Terminal cancellation of a reservation that has not been committed.

post.summary: Commit a reservation into consumed stock
post.description: Converts reserved quantity into a permanent stock reduction and appends COMMIT movement evidence. Repeating a commit does not consume twice.
Moves a HELD reservation to CONFIRMED. Repeating a confirmation does not apply it twice.

post.summary: Release a reservation back to available stock
post.description: Returns reserved quantity to availability. Repeating a release does not release twice, and a release racing expiry settles once.

post.summary: Open a stocktake and snapshot expected quantities
post.description: Captures the expected quantity for each counted item at the moment the stocktake opens. The snapshot is what later variance is measured against.
Closes a stocktake without applying any stock effect.

put.description: Sets the physically counted quantity for one stocktake line.

post.summary: Post a stocktake and apply corrections
post.description: Applies the counted variance as STOCKTAKE_CORRECTION movements. A stocktake whose snapshot is stale relative to current stock is refused rather than allowed to overwrite newer truth, and posting twice does not correct twice.

Source and destination items must represent the same stock identity: same item type, source reference, measure and stock basis mode. Moving stock across differing basis modes would change what the quantity means and is refused.
Marks a transfer ready to dispatch.
Cancels a transfer that has not been received, returning any in-transit stock to the source branch.
Removes stock from the source branch and places it in transit.
Books in-transit stock into the destination branch, recording damaged or missing quantities. Receiving twice does not book the stock twice.

hmacV2.name: X-Service-Signature
hmacV2.description: HMAC v2 service signature. Internal Inventory routes also require X-Service-Name, X-Service-Timestamp and X-Service-Nonce; the nonce is durably consumed so a replayed request is refused.

IdempotencyKey.name: Idempotency-Key
IdempotencyKey.description: Repeat-safe key for a mutating Inventory operation.

available_quantity.description: Sellable quantity. Never negative; excludes quarantined and expired stock.

Movement.description: One immutable ledger entry. Never updated or deleted.

supplier_ref.description: Opaque reference only. Supplier and purchase-order authority belongs to Section 15, not Section 14.
